units.en: For the pre-1.9 occupation system see a previous version of this page.

States are divided into three main categories based on resistance: core states (also known in-game as national territory), occupied states, and colony states. Occupied states have resistance enabled, while colony states do not. If a core state has resistance turned on (whether if the requirement to enable resistance is changed in a mod or an effect forces it to be enabled, such as with the ⟦0⟧ operation), it will be listed as an occupied state, while still not having the mali that apply to non-core states such as with manpower or building slots.

If a state does not have resistance at the start of the game, then it will remain disabled unless the state changes hands⟦0⟧ or another mechanic enables it (such as various ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ that enable resistance in certain colonial states in Africa and Arabia).
If a state changes hands or resistance already exists, the game decides daily whether it should continue by checking the following conditions:⟦0⟧
The state is not a core of the controller country
Either any country has a core on this country or the state was owned by ⟦0⟧ at the game's start and is occupied by a country originating from Spain, after the civil war has ended.
Occupied states have two values attached to them: ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧.
The resistance system is based on the resistance strength, which slowly grows or decays towards the resistance target.

Resistance strength measures the severity of the populace's resistance to the controller's occupation of the state. Upon the state being captured, the initial resistance is set to 1%,⟦0⟧ from where it rises or falls to the ⟦1⟧. If the state shouldn't have resistance any longer, the resistance decays towards 0 by -0.25%⟦2⟧ per day. The resistance strength is capped between 0.01%⟦3⟧ and 100%.⟦4⟧ It affects the debuffs applied to the state, frequency, and severity of resistance actions. When resistance strength reaches certain thresholds, various debuffs begin to apply on a per-state basis:⟦5⟧
Divisions speed: -50% (Only for the controller) Strategic Redeployment Disabled: Yes Local Supplies: -50% (Only for the controller) Division Attrition: +30% (Only for the controller)

Local Factories: -3% Resistance will declare independence on the core states that are being occupied. (Fires the rebellion event in 1 hour) Occupied states will declare independence. This changes their control to the rebelling country (it will be re-established if it doesn't exist or is at peace with the occupier) and grants divisions to it (2–6 per state, based on factory amount).

This changes their control to the rebelling country (it will be re-established if it doesn't exist or is at peace with the occupier) and grants divisions to it (2–6 per state, based on factory amount).

Modifiers or effects, such as the following:⟦0⟧ Compassionate Gentleman political advisor: -5% Root out resistance mission: Base -10%,[20] increased by upgrading the agency or assigning more agents. Each subsequent agent is only 50%x as efficient as the previous one. Spread from a neighbouring state with a higher resistance target, as ⟦0⟧ of the difference. Only one state can be selected to have the spread from, and it picks the highest one. In this case, the difference is calculated between this state's resistance target (before the spread) and the neighbouring state's either resistance target without the spread or only the spread that it received. For example, a state with a 70% resistance target neighbouring a state with a 10% resistance target will increase the latter's total target to 40% by adding half of the difference between 10% and 70%. If another state with a 10% resistance target borders the state now with a 40% target, it will raise to 20% through half of the difference between the 10% base and the 30% spread from the first state.

For example, a state with a 70% resistance target neighbouring a state with a 10% resistance target will increase the latter's total target to 40% by adding half of the difference between 10% and 70%. If another state with a 10% resistance target borders the state now with a 40% target, it will raise to 20% through half of the difference between the 10% base and the 30% spread from the first state.

The resistance target can only fall down to 10%⟦0⟧ with most of these modifiers, only compliance can push it down further to 0. If resistance falls to 0, then the resistance will only be re-enabled once the resistance target reaches 10%⟦1⟧.

If the resistance strength doesn't match up with the resistance target, it will gradually change towards the resistance target. If the resistance strength is rising, this is ⟦0⟧; if it is falling, this is ⟦1⟧. By default, resistance growth increases it by ⟦2⟧ per day, while resistance decay decreases it by ⟦3⟧ per day. Further modifiers to them are applied multiplicatively.
If the country has a claim on the occupied state, the resistance decay is increased by ⟦0⟧. Below 10 resistance strength, decay is changed by ⟦1⟧, while below 20 strength, decay is changed by ⟦2⟧.⟦3⟧
In terms of modifiers, there are the following ways to change it:⟦0⟧
The ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ for governments in exile increases the resistance growth by ⟦2⟧ within the core states of the country with the spirit.
The ⟦0⟧ land doctrine in the ⟦1⟧ doctrine branch increases the resistance growth by ⟦2⟧ within the core states of the country with the doctrine.
The ⟦0⟧ occupation law available to ⟦1⟧ increases the resistance decay by ⟦2⟧ in the states where it's applied to.

Each day that resistance is active, the game rolls for resistance activity. The chance for resistance activity to happen in a state increases by ⟦0⟧ per ⟦1⟧ of resistance in that state, up to a maximum of ⟦2⟧ at ⟦3⟧ resistance.⟦4⟧

Whenever resistance activity happens in a state, local partisans will attack and destroy ⟦0⟧ of the state garrison's equipment and ⟦1⟧ of the state garrison's manpower. Equipment losses are applied to all currently used equipment by the garrison based on the garrison's current fulfillment rate and are rounded up for all equipment types. ⟦2⟧ increases the potential damage to both equipment and manpower. Certain ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧, and ⟦6⟧ can increase or decrease the amount of damage dealt to garrisons in certain occupied states. The garrison template's ⟦7⟧ reduces both types of damage by ⟦8⟧ per ⟦9⟧ hardness, capped at a maximum of ⟦10⟧ at ⟦11⟧ hardness or more. This reduction occurs regardless of the actual equipment the garrison has available.⟦12⟧ For example, a garrison template with a ⟦13⟧ battalion will have its damage reduced even if the country has no heavy tanks to fulfill their garrisons' equipment request. It also stacks additively with other sources of garrison damage reduction up to a maximum total damage reduction of ⟦14⟧.⟦15⟧ This can mean that additional garrison hardness is effectively wasted when enough damage reduction sources from ⟦16⟧, ⟦17⟧, ⟦18⟧, etc. is present.

In addition to damage to garrisons, there is a chance that resistance activity will "penetrate" the garrison and cause damage to local ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, or ⟦2⟧. The base chance is ⟦3⟧ per resistance activity, but this can be increased through ⟦4⟧. Certain unique ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧ can reduce garrison penetration chance.

Compliance is a representation of a non-core territory's population's loyalty to the occupying regime. The in-game number represents the proportion of people in the local population that are loyalists.
Compliance is calculated on a per-state basis with its own local effects while providing overall bonuses for occupied land when reaching a certain average threshold.

Compliance in an occupied state starts at ⟦0⟧. Once a state capitulates or is annexed, if a ⟦1⟧ has been prepared beforehand, starting compliance in all of its original states will increase to the country's collaboration percentage. Non-core states at the beginning of the game start with 70%⟦2⟧ compliance by default. If a non-core state switches owners, its new owner will receive ⟦3⟧⟦4⟧ of the old owner's compliance in that state.

While having access to more than 100% of a state's factories or resources is usually temporary because compliance decay will outgrow compliance gain, there are some situations where this is not the case. Certain ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, and decisions on certain countries can result in a compliance gain that overwhelms the additional compliance decay created by more extractive ⟦2⟧. In particular, the ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧-exclusive ⟦5⟧, and ⟦6⟧-specific ⟦7⟧ occupation laws all provide additional factories and resources while having low enough compliance gain reduction that they can be easily overwhelmed by additional sources of compliance gain.

Fractional factories and resources are rounded down for each individual factory and resource type. On game startup, they are also grouped by tag and have a different rounding procedure, but this is corrected a few days into the game, when factories from occupation are first recalculated.
